This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Ovens River downstream of Rocky Point.
This Watch and Act message replaces message at 12.24 am Wednesday morning. 

Moderate flooding occurring at Wangaratta 
Minor flooding along parts of the King River 
Rainfall since Sunday morning resulted in areas of minor to major flooding. 
The main flood peak is now passing Wangaratta and approaching Peechelba East. 

Ovens River downstream of Rocky Point 
Moderate flooding is occurring at Wangaratta.
The Ovens River at Wangaratta peaked around 12.65 metres around 1 pm Tuesday and is currently 12.56 metres and falling slowly.
The river is likely to remain above the Minor flood level (11.90 metres) throughout Thursday.

King River 
  •  Moderate flooding is estimated to be occurring at Docker Rd Bridge and minor flooding is easing at Lake William Hovell (Downstream). 
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. 
Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • People who live or work along the Ovens River should monitor river levels closely and follow their emergency plan.
  • Farmers downstream of Wangaratta should move livestock and machinery to higher ground if still safe to do so.
  • Rising floodwater can be dangerous. Be aware of water levels rising near you.
  • Campers: If you are camping close to the river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in the Wangaratta area:
  • Yogi was wet between the nose and eyes overnight and will remain in floodwater as the river peak slowly falls. 
  • King River floodwater may still be filling the Kaluna Wetlands into Merriwa Park. 
  • Bickerton Street and Mundgee Place carparks are still flooded.  
  • Painters Island Caravan Park is still closed. 
  • Deep floodwater around Northern Beaches, Sydney Beach, Pinkerton Crescent.
  • Floodwater may still enter backyards and low-lying garages and sheds along the Ovens floodplain north, south and east of Wangaratta, including around the airport, Tarrawingee, Markwood, Oxley Flats, Londrigan, Bowser, Docker Plains and North Wangaratta areas, and in Templeton Street and Baker Street.
  • Many river and creek walking paths and bike tracks will still be closed. 
  • Check the Wangaratta Local Flood Guide for more local impacts and advice www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/flood-guides/rural-city-of-wangaratta#wangaratta-local-flood-guide
Impacts in the Whorouly area: 
  • Widespread Minor level flooding may still be affecting farmland and local access roads.
  •  Local knowledge advises that the Snow Road may still be flooded between the Great Alpine Road and Carboor-Everton Road. The Whorouly Road North of the shop may still be flooded to the Snow Road. The southern access to the Snow Road is safe to use.
Key Road Closures
  • There will be extensive local road closures - drive with care and never enter floodwater. 
  • The Great Alpine Road is closed at Yellow Creek. A detour is in place via Detour Road.Many local roads may be flooded. 
  • For the latest road closures go to:  www.traffic.transport.vic.gov.au and obey ROAD CLOSED signs and follow instructions from emergency services.

  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • If cleaning after damage has occurred, protect your health and safety. Wear strong boots, gloves and protective clothing and wash your hands and clothes regularly.
If your home or business has been flooded:
  • Check for building damage before you enter.
  • Have all electrical and gas equipment professionally tested before use.
  • Clean and dry out the building as soon as possible.
Call Triple Zero (000) in a life threatening emergency. For emergency assistance from the SES call 132 500.
Impacts in your area:
